causes.text: Spirit AeroSystems disclosed a quality issue involving elongated fastener holes on the aft pressure bulkhead on certain 737 fuselage units.

effects.text: Boeing shares fell about 4.5% the following day as delivery targets came under pressure from the supplier defect.

source_info.title: Boeing shares fall as 737 goal at risk from supplier defect involving Spirit

causal_reasoning_chain.description: Supplier discloses a manufacturing non-conformance in fuselage components.
Markets infer delivery delays and higher rework costs.
Boeing shares drop 4.5% on the revised expectations.

rationale: Spirit's statement and subsequent Reuters coverage tied the defect to near-term Boeing delivery risk and a stock decline.
counterfactual_analysis: Absent the supplier defect, investors would expect a steadier 737 delivery cadence.

adversarial_confounders.text: Macro news on the same day
adversarial_confounders.impact: Could have influenced trading alongside the defect headlines.

details.commentary: A critical aerostructures supplier's quality lapse forced Boeing to halt or slow deliveries, revealing how dependent it remained on a concentrated upstream base. That disruption weakened Boeing's own bargaining position and raised the risk of penalties and rework costs, prompting investors to mark down the shares on renewed execution concerns.
